next_task.title: Bounded parallel fetch: polite per-host concurrency over the acquisition boundary
next_task.objective: Fetch a set of approved URLs concurrently under a bounded, per-host polite schedule so that a multi-source question completes faster than a serial fetch while no host receives more than its permitted concurrency, and so that every per-URL result - stored, duplicate, or refused - is a typed outcome rather than a lost task.
prerequisites: M002.5 complete (content-addressed snapshot store with retry-safe deduplication)
M002.2 and M002.3 complete (acquisition policy and per-host robots and politeness)
No sibling code may be copied while the licence gate in docs/REUSE_PROVENANCE.md is unmet
No test may perform real network access, real DNS resolution, or read a live page
Sources/LocalLensCore/Domain.swift Snapshot and Passage definitions are frozen and must not change
M001 deterministic slice evidence must remain byte-identical
Search hits remain discovery metadata and must never be promoted to evidence without a fetched body
allowed_scope: a bounded parallel fetch scheduler over the existing acquisition boundary and snapshot store, with stub transports only
a per-host concurrency limit so politeness is a property of the scheduler rather than of the caller
typed per-URL outcomes covering stored, duplicate, and every refusal already defined by acquisition, robots, and extraction
deterministic result ordering independent of completion order
forbidden_scope: real network calls, real DNS resolution or live page capture in tests
SQLite, FTS5, retrieval, ranking or answer generation
copying sibling source while the licence gate is unmet
UI work beyond the existing shell
done_when: a batch of approved URLs is fetched with more than one fetch in flight at a time, proving the schedule is parallel rather than serial
no host ever has more concurrent fetches than its configured per-host limit, and the limit is enforced by the scheduler rather than trusted from the caller
every URL in the batch produces exactly one typed outcome - stored, duplicate, or a refusal - and no task is dropped or silently retried
results are returned in a deterministic order that does not depend on completion order
a refusal of one URL does not abort the rest of the batch
no test performs network access, DNS resolution, or reads a live page (stub transport and frozen fixtures only)
make gate passes and evidence is recorded in LOCAL_BROWSER_STATE.md

product_contract.citation_definition: A typed link from an answer claim to an exact passage in an immutable snapshot; a URL or search snippet alone is not a citation.

nonnegotiable_invariants: Work on one milestone at a time.
Do not weaken a frozen gate after seeing a result.
Search snippets are discovery metadata and never report evidence.
Every factual Evidence UI field names a known claim ID.
Every accepted claim resolves to exact saved passage evidence.
Model output cannot create trusted IDs, executable UI or arbitrary actions.
Local and hosted results remain visibly and analytically separate.
No model, embedding model or reranker is tested without a measured failure and frozen promotion threshold.
Normal users do not need Docker or a terminal.
Documentation checks do not prove runtime behavior.
Never expose secrets, private snapshots, downloaded weights or restricted benchmark bodies.

conditional_experiments.eligible_only_when: labelled passage-recall failures require document-wide context
candidate recall is adequate but ordering is a measured downstream failure
the bounded single-controller design has a demonstrated product failure

before_work: Inspect the working tree and preserve unrelated changes.
Restate the active milestone, proof level and exact gate.
Do not infer that an existing file is built, tested or accepted.
after_work: Update tests, documentation, project.json and LOCAL_BROWSER_STATE.md together.
State which proof level was actually reached.
Leave exactly one eligible next task.
